lemma: Let W = U A + E over Z with U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= a, and E supported on a column set S with |S| = s <= k, where k is the number of nonzero entries of E. Let F = [n] minus S. For x in {0,1}^n, the row-j dot product is U_j . y(x_F) + sum_{c in S} W_jc x_c with y(x_F) = A_F x_F in Z^r, since W_jc = sum_i U_ji A_ic on F. The count #{x : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} equals the sum over x_S in {0,1}^s of the number of x_F weighted by the value of y, so it is computed exactly by a DP over F with state y, of size at most (2a n + 1)^r, repeated for each x_S. Time 2^s (2an+1)^r poly(m,n) <= 2^k (2an+1)^r poly(m,n). This is a re-derivation of S0002 and does not close G0001(i) for k = Theta(n) or for rank r = Theta(n / log n).
gap: Saving over 2^n needs s <= (1-delta) n and r log2(2an+1) <= delta n. Open: a sparse-E family with k = Theta(n) entries and r = o(n / log n) is covered only when k <= (1-delta) n; the range k in ((1-delta) n, n] is not covered by this bound.
evidence: cm-08de45c96cfe4d30: 1080 runs, n in {6,8,10}, r in {1,2}, k in {1,2,3}, 0 mismatches vs brute force; max DP states / 2^n at most 0.281 (n = 6, r = 2). Scope: n <= 10 only; not an asymptotic claim.
